inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed a bill on Thursday that requires new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. If a South [...] The post South Dakota bill requires new voters to prove US citizenship for state elections appeared first on JURIST - News .
inputs.modified_text: Larry Rhoden has signed Senate Bill 175, putting another paperwork barrier in front of people trying to vote in South Dakota elections. These requirements don’t fall equally: people with fewer resources or less reliable access to documents are more likely to be excluded. Calling it a narrow procedural change obscures the real issue: the state is making individuals bear the cost of inequality instead of removing barriers to political participation. That is voter suppression, not a neutral fix.
